challenges.name: values-text-truthiness-quiz
challenges.title: Text, numbers and truthiness
challenges.description: Predict what Python does with values that arrive as text, before you write the receipt script.

questions.explanation: qty is the one-character string "0", not the number 0. Only the empty string "" is falsy; any non-empty string, including "0", " " and "False", is truthy, so the if branch runs. In that branch qty * 2 repeats the text ("00") instead of doubling a number, and {qty=} prints the expression and the repr of its value, quotes included: qty='0'. Convert first (int(qty)) and both the test and the arithmetic behave like numbers.

options.text: TypeError: can't multiply sequence by non-int of type 'str'

questions.question: Which of these expressions raise an error? (Select all that apply.)
questions.explanation: int() accepts surrounding whitespace, so int(" 42 ") is 42, but it does not accept a decimal point: int("12.5") raises ValueError: invalid literal for int() with base 10: '12.5'. float() does not understand thousands separators, so float("1,050") raises ValueError too. "Total: " + 3 raises TypeError: can only concatenate str (not "int") to str, because + never converts a number to text for you; str(3) or an f-string does. f"{1050000:,}" is fine and gives '1,050,000'.

challenges.name: aligned-chat-receipt
challenges.title: Write build_receipt(text) for the sales chat
challenges.description: Staff paste order lines into the team chat as "name | quantity | unit price", with messy spacing and prices like "210,000", "210.000" or "35.000 đ". Turn every valid line into one aligned receipt line (name cut or padded to 16, quantity in 3, price in 9 and amount in 11 with "," thousands separators), add a TOTAL line that ends under the amount column, and list the line numbers of invalid lines in "skipped" instead of crashing. Blank lines are ignored. The exact rules and column layout are in the starter's docstring; the runner prints your dict as JSON.
